problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 1
problems.problemText:
Bridget bought a bag of apples at the grocery store. She gave half of the apples to Ann. Then she gave Cassie $3$ apples, keeping $4$ apples for herself. How many apples did Bridget buy?

**(A)** $3$ **(B)** $4$ **(C)** $7$ **(D)** $11$ **(E)** $14$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 2
problems.problemText:
On average, for every $4$ sports cars sold at the local dealership, $7$ sedans are sold. The dealership predicts that it will sell $28$ sports cars next month. How many sedans does it expect to sell?

**(A)** $7$ **(B)** $32$ **(C)** $35$ **(D)** $49$ **(E)** $112$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 3
problems.problemText:
The graph shows the constant rate at which Suzanna rides her bike. If she rides a total of a half an hour at the same speed, how many miles would she have ridden?

![Distance-versus-time graph for Suzanna, marked at5,10,15,20 minutes and1,2,3,4 miles.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p3.png)

**(A)** $5$   **(B)** $5.5$   **(C)** $6$   **(D)** $6.5$   **(E)** $7$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 4
problems.problemText:
The five pieces shown below can be arranged to form four of the five figures shown in the choices. Which figure cannot be formed?

![Five straight pieces of lengths1 through5, followed by the five candidate grid figures A through E.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p4.png)

**(A)** figure A   **(B)** figure B   **(C)** figure C   **(D)** figure D   **(E)** figure E

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 5
problems.problemText:
A sequence of numbers starts with $1$, $2$, and $3$. The fourth number of the sequence is the sum of the previous three numbers in the sequence: $1+2+3=6$. In the same way, every number after the fourth is the sum of the previous three numbers. What is the eighth number in the sequence?

**(A)** $11$   **(B)** $20$   **(C)** $37$   **(D)** $68$   **(E)** $99$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 6
problems.problemText:
Steve's empty swimming pool will hold $24,000$ gallons of water when full. It will be filled by $4$ hoses, each of which supplies $2.5$ gallons of water per minute. How many hours will it take to fill Steve's pool?

**(A)** $40$ **(B)** $42$ **(C)** $44$ **(D)** $46$ **(E)** $48$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 7
problems.problemText:
The triangular plot of $ACD$ lies between Aspen Road, Brown Road and a railroad. Main Street runs east and west, and the railroad runs north and south. The numbers in the diagram indicate distances in miles. The width of the railroad track can be ignored. How many square miles are in the plot of land $ACD$?

![Aspen Road and Brown Road from A meet the railroad at C and D; AB, BC, and CD are each marked3 miles.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p7.png)

**(A)** $2$   **(B)** $3$   **(C)** $4.5$   **(D)** $6$   **(E)** $9$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 8
problems.problemText:
The length of a rectangle is increased by $10\%$ and the width is decreased by $10\%$. What percent of the old area is the new area?

**(A)** $90$ **(B)** $99$ **(C)** $100$ **(D)** $101$ **(E)** $110$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 9
problems.problemText:
A triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, and octagon are joined in a chain, each neighboring pair sharing one side. How many sides are on the outside boundary of the resulting figure?

![Initial three members of the polygon chain: an equilateral triangle, square, and regular pentagon, with shared edges dashed.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p9.png)

**(A)** $21$ **(B)** $23$ **(C)** $25$ **(D)** $27$ **(E)** $29$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 10
problems.problemText:
On a checkerboard composed of $64$ unit squares, what is the probability that a randomly chosen unit square does not touch the outer edge of the board?

![Eight-by-eight checkerboard with alternating black and white unit squares.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p10.png)

**(A)** $\frac{1}{16}$   **(B)** $\frac{7}{16}$   **(C)** $\frac{1}{2}$   **(D)** $\frac{9}{16}$   **(E)** $\frac{49}{64}$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 11
problems.problemText:
The Amaco Middle School bookstore sells pencils costing a whole number of cents. Some seventh graders each bought a pencil, paying a total of \$1.43. Some of the $30$ sixth graders each bought a pencil, and they paid a total of \$1.95. How many more sixth graders than seventh graders bought a pencil?

**(A)** $1$ **(B)** $2$ **(C)** $3$ **(D)** $4$ **(E)** $5$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 12
problems.problemText:
One spinner has equally likely outcomes $1,3,5$, and a second spinner has equally likely outcomes $2,4,6$. What is the probability that the sum of the two spins is prime?

![Two spinners split into three equal sectors labeled1,3,5 and2,4,6, with pointer arrows.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p12.png)

**(A)** $\frac12$ **(B)** $\frac23$ **(C)** $\frac34$ **(D)** $\frac79$ **(E)** $\frac56$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 13
problems.problemText:
How many three-digit numbers can be formed using the digits $1,3,$ and $5$ each exactly once and are divisible by $5$? What fraction of all such numbers is this?

**(A)** $\frac16$ **(B)** $\frac13$ **(C)** $\frac12$ **(D)** $\frac23$ **(E)** $\frac56$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 14
problems.problemText:
Austin and Temple are $50$ miles apart along Interstate $35$. Bonnie drove from Austin to her daughter's house in Temple, averaging $60$ miles per hour. Leaving the car with her daughter, Bonnie rode a bus back to Austin along the same route and averaged $40$ miles per hour on the return trip. What was the average speed for the round trip, in miles per hour?

**(A)** $46$ **(B)** $48$ **(C)** $50$ **(D)** $52$ **(E)** $54$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 15
problems.problemText:
A recipe that makes $5$ servings of hot chocolate requires $2$ squares of chocolate, $\frac14$ cup sugar, $1$ cup water, and $4$ cups milk. Jordan has $5$ squares of chocolate, $2$ cups of sugar, lots of water, and $7$ cups of milk. If she maintains the same ratio of ingredients, what is the greatest number of servings of hot chocolate she can make?

**(A)** $5\frac18$ **(B)** $6\frac14$ **(C)** $7\frac12$ **(D)** $8\frac34$ **(E)** $9\frac78$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 16
problems.problemText:
How many three-digit positive integers have digits whose product is $24$?

**(A)** $12$ **(B)** $15$ **(C)** $18$ **(D)** $21$ **(E)** $24$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 17
problems.problemText:
The product $360x$ is a perfect square, and $360y$ is a perfect cube, where $x$ and $y$ are positive integers. What is the least possible value of $x+y$?

**(A)** $80$ **(B)** $85$ **(C)** $95$ **(D)** $105$ **(E)** $115$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 18
problems.problemText:
A $7\times7$ floor has black tiles arranged in alternating horizontal and vertical strips as shown. The same pattern is continued on a $15\times15$ floor. How many white tiles are on the $15\times15$ floor?

![Seven-by-seven floor pattern with black alternating rows and columns and white corners.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p18.png)

**(A)** $49$ **(B)** $57$ **(C)** $64$ **(D)** $96$ **(E)** $126$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 19
problems.problemText:
In an isosceles triangle, one angle has measure $70^\circ$. What is the sum of all possible values of the measure of another angle of the triangle?

**(A)** $95$ **(B)** $110$ **(C)** $125$ **(D)** $165$ **(E)** $180$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 20
problems.problemText:
Eight points are arranged as the vertices of a $3\times1$ rectangular grid. How many noncongruent triangles can be formed by choosing three of the points?

![Eight points in two equally spaced horizontal rows of four points each.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p20.png)

**(A)** $5$ **(B)** $6$ **(C)** $7$ **(D)** $8$ **(E)** $9$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 21
problems.problemText:
Andy and Bethany have a rectangular array of numbers greater than $0$ with $40$ rows and $75$ columns. Andy adds the numbers in each row. The average of his $40$ sums is $A$. Bethany adds the numbers in each column. The average of her $75$ sums is $B$. What is the value of $\frac{A}{B}$?

**(A)** $\frac{64}{225}$ **(B)** $\frac8{15}$ **(C)** $1$ **(D)** $\frac{15}{8}$ **(E)** $\frac{225}{64}$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 22
problems.problemText:
How many whole numbers between $1$ and $1000$ do not contain the digit $1$?

**(A)** $512$ **(B)** $648$ **(C)** $720$ **(D)** $728$ **(E)** $800$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 23
problems.problemText:
On the last day of school, Mrs. Awesome gave jelly beans to her class. She gave each boy as many jelly beans as there were boys in the class. She gave each girl as many jelly beans as there were girls in the class. She brought $400$ jelly beans, and when she finished, she had six jelly beans left. There were two more boys than girls in her class. How many students were in her class?

**(A)** $26$ **(B)** $28$ **(C)** $30$ **(D)** $32$ **(E)** $34$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 24
problems.problemText:
In the cryptarithm shown, $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are different digits:

![Two vertical cryptarithms: AB plus CA equals DA, and AB minus CA equals A.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p24.png)

What is the value of $D$?

**(A)** $5$ **(B)** $6$ **(C)** $7$ **(D)** $8$ **(E)** $9$

problems.title: 2009 AMC 8 Problem 25
problems.problemText:
A one-cubic-foot cube is cut into four pieces by three cuts parallel to the top face of the cube. The first cut is $\frac{1}{2}$ foot from the top face. The second cut is $\frac{1}{3}$ foot below the first cut, and the third cut is $\frac{1}{17}$ foot below the second cut. From the top to the bottom the pieces are labeled A, B, C, and D. The pieces are then glued together end to end as shown in the second diagram. What is the total surface area of this solid in square feet?

![Unit cube divided into horizontal slabs A,B,C,D, with cuts labeled one-half, one-third, one-seventeenth; slabs are rejoined in order C,B,A,D.](/problem-images/amc8/2009/p25.png)

**(A)** $6$   **(B)** $7$   **(C)** $\frac{419}{51}$   **(D)** $\frac{158}{17}$   **(E)** $11$
